title: Make the explainer site introduce Athena and firstmate to newcomers
summary: The site is a page about firstmate rendered by xtask/src/site.rs from the study's JSON. I read the rating as asking for: an Athena and study introduction up front, a clearer firstmate definition, links for the repo and sources, the glossary moved lower, and generator jargon removed from the limits section. Readers are newcomers to the site.

defaults_applied.how: The xtask site tests are updated and cargo test and clippy must pass.
The generator and intro data are fixed, not the published HTML.
One focused change to the site generator and its intro data.
The page copy is written for an outside reader.
No personal data goes into the page or links.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The audience is a newcomer who opens the site root and knows neither Athena nor firstmate.
Athena's repository link is derivable from the repo, README or Cargo metadata; the producer will choose a stable link.
Claim citations stay, since the site's design requires them, but they are made less intrusive and sources become links.
No workflow change is needed because pages.yml already builds the site from xtask.

acceptance_criteria.text: The rendered page's title, heading and opening paragraph name Athena, say what Athena is, and say who made the study and why, before firstmate is discussed.
The page says what firstmate is in plain words, including that its workers are AI coding agents, who would use it, and what problem it solves. The page also explains what a study is.
The pinned repository URL is an HTML link, and each claim source is a link to the pinned commit's file and lines when the repository is on GitHub. The link text is HTML-escaped.
The glossary appears after the walk-through and states, not before. The vague captain entry is clarified or removed.
The Limits section does not show internal field names such as guard_evaluated_by, and the guard-none note reads in plain language.
The page includes a next-steps section that links to Athena and to firstmate.
Run cargo test --workspace and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets. Both pass, including updated xtask site tests that check the new order and links.
Run cargo run -p xtask -- site. It still succeeds, and every element still cites an existing claim.

out_of_scope: Changing the firstmate study's claims or re-running the study
Changing the audience rating mechanism or records/
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass rate than the reference: the work spans generator code, study JSON and tests, with several copy changes to check.
